summary: Practise records classification, retention, metadata, and digital preservation workflows. Explore the five-day course and review the outline.
lede: Electronic records management training helps records staff and digital archivists control records from capture through retention, transfer, and preservation. Participants practise building inventories and classification schemes, creating metadata profiles, making retention decisions, checking file formats, and documenting transfer and migration quality.
audienceIntro: This foundation course is designed for staff who handle electronic records, digital collections, metadata, retention, transfer, or preservation in their daily work. This course is designed for: Records Managers maintaining classification, retention, and disposition controls. Electronic Records Managers coordinating capture and retrieval in business systems. Digital Archivists arranging and describing born-digital and digitized collections. Digital Preservation Specialists assessing file-format risks and migration outcomes. Records Officers advising teams on inventories, access, and lifecycle requirements. ERMS administrators configuring classification and metadata fields for records capture. Digitization coordinators checking image files against agreed quality criteria. Information governance officers aligning records schedules with business-unit ownership. Archives technicians documenting digital accessions and preparing finding aids. Microsoft 365 administrators supporting records controls in SharePoint, Teams, and OneDrive.
prerequisites: No coding or programming is required. Familiarity with routine records handling, business systems, shared workspaces, or digital collections will help you apply the exercises to your work. Bring a laptop if available; the course can use supplied examples and templates, with access to specialist tools depending on the delivery setup.
